findings.description: T-002 tells the worker to do the one thing B-2's arithmetic forbids, and the collision propagates into V-2. T-002 says of `doctor.bats:244`: "Build it out of helper calls if that reads cleanly; that is encouraged, not penalised." The constitution says "**exactly 52 assertions call a shared helper** — not 'at least 52'." A worker who takes the encouragement produces 53 helper-calling assertions (or 54 call lines), and B-2's checker, told the number is exact and warned that "an off-by-one here misdirects every checker", fails work that followed its task file to the letter. It does not stop there. V-2 part 2 requires `doctor.bats` to contribute **exactly 20** sites; a form-recognising `mutation-check.sh` scanning a `:244` built from two helper calls counts 21. And V-2's two mutation rules then both claim those lines — the polarity rule (`assert_not_contains` becomes `assert_contains`) and the disjunction rule (replace both needles with a sentinel) — so the script has no defined behaviour there. Three artifacts disagree about one line. This is the "exactly 52" minor from CON-audit r1 coming home: it was deferred as a post-PASS amendment, and the decomposition has now taken the trapped side, so it has to be settled before dispatch. The cheap fix is one edit in T-002 — require `:244` to be a plain `if` over `case`/`grep`/`[ ]` and say helper calls are not permitted there — which keeps 52 exact, keeps doctor at 20 recognisable sites, and keeps the two mutation rules disjoint. The alternative costs three edits: B-2's count, V-2 part 2's doctor figure, and V-2's form-recognition rule.
findings.evidence: T-002.md:70 (`Build it out of helper calls if that reads cleanly; that is encouraged, not penalised`) against constitution.md:191 (`So **exactly 52 assertions call a shared helper** — not "at least 52" — and all 53 are mutated by V-2`), constitution.md:281 and T-007.md:39 (`doctor 20`), and constitution.md:268-269 (the two mutation rules). Verified at 61213fe: tests/doctor.bats:244 is `[[ "$output" == *"undeclared"* || "$output" == *"casks"* ]]`, the suite's only disjunction, and doctor.bats holds exactly 20 first-token sites.

findings.description: T-007 gives the worker no rule for telling a converted assertion from a pre-existing one, and the file that makes this bite is the one file the task never mentions. **`tests/install-failures.bats` already contains 30 `assert_contains`/`assert_not_contains` call sites** — measured — and after T-001 wires it to `tests/helpers.bash` those 30 are indistinguishable in form from the 53 conversions. T-007 says "For each of the **53** converted assertions" and lists six files with counts, but never states that `install-failures.bats` is excluded, never says why (its calls predate this job and were never `[[ ]]`), and never says how the script decides what to enumerate. The cheapest correct-looking implementation — glob `tests/*.bats`, recognise helper-call forms — finds 82 sites and fails V-2 part 2 on its first run, having done nothing wrong that its task file told it about. V-2 part 2 is an exact-count check with no tolerance, so this is a guaranteed rework rather than a risk of one. `tests/lint.bats` is a smaller second instance: T-006 does not forbid it from calling helpers, and it is absent from T-007's six-file list too. Fix: state the allowlist explicitly in T-007 — apps, doctor, font, jsonc, licensed-fonts, packages, and only those — and name install-failures.bats's 30 pre-existing calls as the reason the allowlist has to exist.
findings.evidence: Measured, and now live: T-001 has landed, so those calls already resolve to the shared `tests/helpers.bash`. `/usr/bin/grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*(assert_contains|assert_not_contains)[[:space:]]' tests/install-failures.bats` -> **30**; the same pattern returns 0 for each of the other six files. T-007.md:37-39 against constitution.md:281 (V-2 part 2's exact per-file counts) and T-001.md:50 (which adds a `load` to install-failures.bats, pointing its 30 calls at the shared helpers).

findings.description: Answering your question 5: the concurrency is a real hazard, and the fix is a dep edge pointing the opposite way from the obvious one. T-006 and T-007 both depend only on T-002..T-005, so they may run together. If T-006 lands first, `tests/lint.bats` scans a `tests/mutation-check.sh` that does not exist yet, and `grep` against a missing operand exits **2** — measured. A guard written the natural way, asserting the scan found nothing via a non-zero status, treats exit 2 as clean and **passes vacuously**, with its coverage of a third of the guarded surface never verified; a stricter guard fails and T-006's worker takes a FAIL it did not earn. V-1 part 2 compounds it: planting 3 appends to a nonexistent `tests/mutation-check.sh`, creating it, and the restore `cp "$REPO/tests/mutation-check.sh" tests/` has no source to copy from. The reverse ordering is wanted too, for an independent reason — if `lint.bats` exists when T-007's script enumerates sites, any helper call inside it inflates the count V-2 part 2 pins. Both point the same way: **T-007 before T-006**. Add T-007 to T-006's `deps`. Non-circular, and nearly free in wall-clock, since T-007 is the long pole either way.
findings.evidence: T-006.md:20 (`deps: [T-002, T-003, T-004, T-005]`) and T-007.md:26 (identical), against T-006.md:31-37 (the three globs the guard must scan, including tests/mutation-check.sh) and constitution.md:210-251 (V-1's planting block). Measured: `/usr/bin/grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*(\[\[|\(\()' tests/*.bats tests/helpers.bash tests/mutation-check.sh` with the two non-`.bats` files absent -> exit 2, no stdout.

findings.description: B-1's surface is checked file by file across seven tasks, and one file falls between them. The constitution states the check as a single command over `tests/*.bats tests/helpers.bash tests/mutation-check.sh`; the decomposition splits it — helpers.bash to T-001, doctor/font/apps to T-002/3/4, jsonc+licensed-fonts+packages to T-005, lint.bats to T-006, mutation-check.sh to T-007. **`tests/install-failures.bats` is named in no task's B-1 grep**, verified across all nine files. It is not an idle omission: T-001 edits that file (deletes the local definitions at :73-83, adds a `load`) and T-008 may edit its comments again, so it is a file this job touches twice with nothing running B-1 against it. The coverage does exist transitively once `lint.bats` lands and T-009 runs `bats tests/`, which is why this is major rather than blocker — but no `check_method` states it, and T-009 does not cite B-1 at all. Add B-1 to T-009's clauses with the constitution's own full-surface command. One grep, and the surface stops having a seam.
findings.evidence: Measured: `/usr/bin/grep -n 'grep -nE.*install-failures' .agent-guild/state/tasks/*.md` -> no match. install-failures.bats appears in T-001, T-006, T-008 and T-009 but never inside a first-token `[[` check. T-001.md:15 scopes its B-1 check to `tests/helpers.bash` alone; T-009.md:9-21 cites V-3, D-1, D-3 only. constitution.md:172 for the single full-surface command.

findings.description: Three of the four conversion tables give line numbers without saying they are baseline numbers, and this has already happened rather than being a risk. T-001 landed while this audit was running, and it added two lines to the top of every test file — a `load 'helpers'` plus a blank — so **every site in every table is now off by exactly +2**, measured across all six files. A worker opening the current `font.bats` and going to "line 310" lands two lines above the site. T-002 gets this right ("**The 20 sites, at baseline line numbers**") and so do the inline blocks in T-003 and T-004 (`# :500 baseline`, `# :135`) and T-005's licensed-fonts and packages tables, whose column is headed "baseline". What is missing is the label on T-003's ten-site table, T-004's six-site table, and T-005's jsonc table. The needles are distinctive enough that a worker recovers, so this is a stumble rather than a defect — one word in three places, or a uniform +2 if you would rather restate the numbers as they now stand.
findings.evidence: Measured after T-001 landed: first site per file, baseline -> now — doctor :97 -> :99, font :115 -> :117, apps :135 -> :137, jsonc :61 -> :63, licensed-fonts :46 -> :48, packages :117 -> :119. Delta is +2 in all six. Site counts are unchanged (apps 11, doctor 20, font 12, jsonc 2, licensed-fonts 5, packages 4 = 54). T-003.md:39-50, T-004.md:39-46, T-005.md:37-40 against T-002.md:37.

findings.description: T-006 never says how many cases `tests/lint.bats` should contribute, and V-1's mutation block reads most naturally against exactly one. The block says "the guard case MUST report `not ok`" in the singular three times, and T-006's own verify step runs `bats tests/lint.bats` expecting a single pass/fail signal — but nothing tells the worker whether one case covering all three globs or one case per glob is wanted, and a three-case file makes "MUST report not ok" ambiguous about which case. Nothing downstream breaks either way, since T-009's floors explicitly say "plus whatever `tests/lint.bats` adds", so this is a wording gap rather than a coverage one.
findings.evidence: T-006.md:27-63 against constitution.md:219-255 (V-1's check, singular throughout) and T-009.md:42 (`119 across the seven pre-existing files, plus whatever tests/lint.bats adds`).

findings.description: T-007 never states outright that the script must map an assertion to its enclosing `@test` name, which is the capability the whole clause turns on. It is implied twice — "require **that specific case** to report `not ok`" and "confirm the case you mutated reports `not ok` by name" — so a careful worker infers that block-aware parsing of `@test` boundaries is required. But it is the least obvious requirement in the task and the one part 4 exists to verify, and it deserves a sentence rather than an inference, especially at sonnet.
findings.evidence: T-007.md:37 and T-007.md:49 against T-007.md:41-45 (the mutation rule, which is stated explicitly) — the contrast is that every other capability is spelled out and this one is not.

findings.description: Answering question 1: your mapping holds, every criterion has a task behind it, and no task does work the spec did not ask for. AC1 (no bare `[[ ]]`, all 54 replaced with a helper) -> T-001 for the helpers plus T-002..T-005 for the conversions, and the arithmetic closes exactly: doctor 20 + font 12 + apps 11 + (jsonc 2 + licensed-fonts 5 + packages 4) = 54. AC2 -> T-006. AC3 -> T-001 via B-3 part 3, which is the right home: AC3 is a verification criterion rather than a deliverable, so it belongs in a `check_method` and not in a build task. AC4 -> T-007. AC5 -> T-009. On the other side of the ledger, T-008 is invited by the spec directly (`_working-memory/conventions.md` carries the existing rules for it, and this belongs alongside them) and T-009's commit work is house standard under D-3; nothing else reaches past the spec.
findings.evidence: spec.md:88-92 against T-001.md:5, T-002.md:5, T-003.md:5, T-004.md:5, T-005.md:5, T-006.md:5, T-007.md:5, T-008.md:5, T-009.md:5. spec.md:108 for D-2's invitation. Site counts re-derived at 61213fe per file: apps 11, doctor 20, font 12, install-failures 0, jsonc 2, licensed-fonts 5, packages 4.

findings.description: Answering question 4, and the part of it that mattered most: **all four per-site conversion tables are exact.** I checked every one of the 54 entries against the files at 61213fe — line number, baseline text, needle, and polarity. T-002's 20 doctor lines all match, including the four `!=` sites at 140/175/195/228 that the task flags as the polarity trap. T-003's ten straightforward needles match, `:115` correctly keeps the `$active_family` interpolation, and both computed-haystack conversions are right: `:500` maps the jq output to the haystack argument and `:554` maps `$fallback` to the needle and `$terminal_family` to the haystack, which is the direction a worker would most plausibly get backwards. T-004's six `$output` needles and all five `registry_line` conversions match, including `:190`'s trailing comma, and its note that `--adopt` and `--machine` are safe because `assert_contains` uses `grep -qF --` is correct. T-005's eleven match, including `:117`'s single-quoted `brew "age"` and the `:62`/`:63` adjacent-opposite pair it calls out. The two ancillary counts are right too: a naive `grep '\[\['` returns 12 over apps.bats (11 commands plus the `grep -oE` regex at :50) and five non-command hits across the suite. Nothing in these tables would propagate a wrong needle.
findings.evidence: Re-derived with `/usr/bin/grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*(\[\[|\(\()' tests/<file>` for all seven files and compared entry by entry against T-002.md:39-60, T-003.md:39-64, T-004.md:39-61, T-005.md:35-58. Ancillary: `/usr/bin/grep -c '\[\[' tests/apps.bats` -> 12. Case counts cited by the tasks all reproduce: doctor 11, font 44, apps 18, jsonc 9, licensed-fonts 7, packages 13, and T-005's combined 29.

findings.description: Answering question 4's actual question — the two weakest excerpts are **T-007 and T-006**, and both weaknesses are recorded above rather than being matters of prose. T-007 is weakest: a worker must guess the enumeration boundary (blocker 2) and infer the `@test`-mapping requirement (minor). Everything else in it is unusually complete — the mutation rule is fixed, the TAP failure mode is spelled out with the exact bats output, the restore contract carries its reason in both directions, and the cost budget is given. T-006 is second: it inherits the sequencing hazard (major) and leaves the case count open (minor), but its statement of what to scan, why first-token is non-negotiable, and why `BATS_TEST_DIRNAME` matters is precise. The other seven stand alone. T-001 in particular is the strongest of the nine — it ships the exact helper bodies rather than describing them, explains the two-argument default that T-003 and T-004 depend on, and forbids starting the conversions that belong to later tasks.

Answering question 2: no split, no merge, and the per-file split is right for a better reason than the one you gave. T-002 is one dispatch — 19 of its 20 sites are table lookups against a table I verified line by line, and the twentieth is a bounded restructure; its risk is the polarity trap, not its size, and that trap is named in the task with its own failing example. T-007 should not split either, because splitting would put an artifact boundary inside a single shell script, which is worse than a large task; its risk is difficulty, which is a routing question rather than a decomposition one. The four conversion tasks should stay split, and the argument is stronger than V-2's counts lining up: a FAIL on doctor does not re-dispatch font, each task gets a clean single-file B-1 grep and its own per-file case floor, and the four can run concurrently after T-001. T-005 bundling three files slightly breaks the symmetry, but its `check_method` names all three per-file counts, so the alignment survives.
findings.evidence: T-002.md:39-60 (the 20-row table, verified exact), T-007.md:41-57 (six interacting requirements in one script), T-005.md:9-18 (the three-file check_method naming 2, 5 and 4 sites and 9, 7 and 13 cases).

findings.description: Answering question 3. **The conversion tasks are correctly at sonnet.** Against haiku: the tables are complete, but T-002's `:244` needs a restructure and T-004's five `registry_line` sites need nested single-inside-double quoting where a slip yields a silently wrong needle — neither is the zero-judgment work `worker-bulk` is for. Against opus: a blocker-severity trap argues for a strong *checker*, not a strong executor, and `checker-judgment` at opus reading 53 before/after pairs against `git show 61213fe:<file>` catches a polarity slip by direct comparison rather than by insight. Sonnet with that checker, plus the ladder, is the right economics. **T-007 at sonnet is defensible and I would open at opus.** The asymmetry with the conversion tasks is that T-007's checker is `checker-deterministic`: it runs four scripted parts and cannot read the script for contract compliance, so there is no judgment backstop the way B-2 backstops T-002. Against that, six interacting requirements in one script, and each failed dispatch costs a roughly six-minute check to discover. The ladder does work here — but it would spend two sonnet dispatches and two long checks learning what the task's own description already says about its difficulty. If blocker 2 is fixed, sonnet becomes materially more plausible; I would still start a rung up on the job's load-bearing deliverable.
findings.evidence: T-002.md:6-8, T-004.md:48-63, T-007.md:6-8 and :9-22 against the routing table in .agent-guild/CLAUDE.md. Checker routing itself is consistent: every deterministic-only task (T-001, T-006, T-007) takes checker-deterministic, every task citing a judgment clause (T-002..T-005 on B-2, T-008 on D-2, T-009 on D-3) takes checker-judgment, and the mixed tasks correctly take the judgment checker, which can also run a grep.

findings.description: The mechanical properties you asked me not to spend the audit on all hold, and every factual claim in the task files that I could re-derive reproduces. All nine constitution clauses appear in some task's `clauses`; the dep graph is acyclic (T-001 -> T-002..005 -> {T-006, T-007} -> T-008 -> T-009) and every referenced task exists; each `check_method` names a check for each clause it cites. Beyond that: T-008's claim that decisionLog runs newest-first with 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-07 as its two most recent entries is exact; conventions.md does carry bash 3.2 rules to sit alongside; T-007's per-file runtime figures (apps 6s, doctor 7s, font 12s, jsonc 0.5s, licensed-fonts 1.4s, packages 2s) match measurement within noise; T-001's helper bodies are verbatim what sits at tests/install-failures.bats:73-83; T-003's note that tests/font.bats:552 already uses `[ -n "$fallback" ] || continue` is correct, which is what makes T-005's conversion of packages.bats:146 a precedent rather than an invention.
findings.evidence: `_working-memory/decisionLog.md` headings: `## 2026-08-08 — Gate OS-incompatible packages...` then `## 2026-08-07 — brew fails in two phases...`. `/usr/bin/grep -c '3\.2' _working-memory/conventions.md` -> 2. Measured per-file bats runtimes: 6.3, 6.8, 11.5, 6.1, 0.5, 1.5, 1.9 seconds. tests/font.bats:552 is `[ -n "$fallback" ] || continue`; :554 is the loop-carried site.

findings.description: A note on timing, since it bears on what is still cheap to change. T-001 was dispatched and reached `checking` while this audit was running, and its deliverable is correct as far as I can see from the tree: `load 'helpers'` in all seven files, `tests/helpers.bash` created carrying the explanatory comment moved from install-failures.bats:67-72, and the two local definitions removed. That is T-001's task file executed faithfully. Both blockers above land on tasks that have not been dispatched — T-002 and T-007 — so both are still fixable in the task files rather than in rework. The sequencing major (T-006's deps) and the B-1 seam (T-009's clauses) are likewise untouched by anything that has run.
findings.evidence: `git status --porcelain` shows seven modified test files and `?? tests/helpers.bash`; `git diff --stat` shows +2 lines in each of six files and -18/+2 in install-failures.bats. T-001.md status is `checking`; T-002 through T-009 are all `pending`.
